title: The Object types dialog reflows when a chip is selected, sliding Apply down under the pointer
summary: Confirmed real. The 7 FilterChips sit in a Wrap; Material's default leading checkmark widened the selected chip by 20 logical px, which pushed the Wrap from 2 rows to 3 and moved the Clear/Apply row down. Set showCheckmark: false — selection is already carried by the chip's fill and outline, so the chip is the same width in both states and the action row cannot move. The dialog body was extracted to _showObjectTypeDialog + a @visibleForTesting seam (same pattern as the existing showAngleSliderForTest) because PlannerScreen runs a 1 s sky clock and never settles.

title: Constellation filter is an unsearchable list of 3-letter abbreviations
summary: Confirmed real: _ConstellationDropdown built a DropdownButton with one row per constellation present in tonight's candidates, each labelled 'Constellation: <Abbr>'. Replaced with a _ControlChip that opens a searchable dialog (consistent with every other filter in that row): rows read 'Canes Venatici (CVn)', sorted by full name, with a search field that matches either spelling, a live count of how many constellations tonight's candidates actually cover, and an explicit 'Any constellation' action. The abbreviation->name table was a PRIVATE map inside skotiq_planetarium's OpenNGC catalog; it is now the shared constellation_names.dart (constellationFullName()) and catalog.dart delegates to it, so there is one spelling of 'Canes Venatici' in the app. The finding's ask for 'only constellations with candidates tonight' was already true (availableConstellationsProvider derives from the suggestion set).

title: The Rationale block never names the target it is explaining (and calls a target with no frames a "large unfinished dataset")
summary: Both halves confirmed real. (1) session_optimizer_service.dart:527 gated the line on `primary.dataProgress < 0.25`, and dataProgress is EXACTLY 0.0 when nothing has been captured (target_suggestion_service._calculateDataProgress returns 0.1 for the 'some data, no plan' case), so a target with zero frames was sold as a 'large unfinished dataset' and an 'efficient completion target' in the same block that said 'No data collected yet'. Now gated on `> 0 && < 0.25` and reworded to 'Partially captured already...'. (2) The Rationale SectionHeader read 'Why this plan was chosen' while the numbers under it always belong to plan.primaryTarget — which is NOT the hero card whenever a search or filter leaves a different card on screen. The subtitle now names the target ('Why NGC 6015 was chosen'). I did NOT move the block above the candidate list: that is a layout preference, not a truth defect.

title: Getting a target into the scheduler is a three-deep dead end; every empty state points at another empty state
summary: The dead end is real and I reproduced it in the code: the Add Target sheet (project_dialogs.dart) was a picker over `allDbTargetsProvider` ONLY, and with an empty library it rendered 'No targets in the catalog / Add targets to your library first' with no action — while the only writer of the targets table reachable from the UI was Framing -> Save target (framing_provider.saveTarget) and the plan-tonight sequencer helper. The sheet now also searches the installed sky catalogs (new `installedCatalogSearchProvider` in core — the existing plannerInstalledCatalogSearchProvider deliberately HIDES tonight's candidates, which is exactly backwards for adding one) and creates the library row itself via TargetLibraryService.ensureCatalogTarget (host-aware and dedup-safe), then returns the new id so the caller attaches it to the open project. Rows already in the library are filtered out of the catalog section so an object never appears twice, the row shows type/mag/constellation, and an in-flight add disables the list so a double tap cannot double-create. The empty state now says what to do ('Search for an object by name or catalog id') instead of pointing elsewhere.

title: Scheduler moon avoidance is illumination-only; the app has moon separation everywhere else
summary: Confirmed: TargetConstraintKind had timeWindow / moonIlluminationMax / customHorizon / scheduledWindow and nothing separation-based, so the wizard's 'Moon avoidance' step offered exactly one knob whose semantics are backwards for the common cases (rejects a target 150 deg from a 90% moon, accepts one 10 deg from a 40% moon). Added `moonSeparationMin` end to end: enum + `moonSeparationMinDeg` field + payload encode/decode (payload_json, so no schema migration) + engine evaluation in the same hard-constraint loop as the others, reusing the engine's existing Meeus moon ephemeris and angular-separation helper, with a rejection reason that states the actual separation and the moon's phase. UI: a new 'Moon separation' wizard card + 0-180 deg field + review sentence + row label, and the illumination card was renamed from the over-broad 'Moon avoidance' to 'Moon illumination' now that the pair exists. Default 30 deg. NOT done and left as a decision: the illumination-scaled Lorentzian curve (NINA's) and the missing min-altitude / max-airmass / meridian-side kinds — see the needs-decision item below.
